location: ch04-self-assessment-EN.tex / Section: Reading the results: trajectory selection matrix (sec:sa-results), intro paragraph and Table tab:sa-trajectory
proposedGenericDecision: Replace the named dominant vendor with a role-based descriptor: 'brownfield single-vendor-dominant' or 'brownfield dominant-commercial-suite-centric'. The trajectory taxonomy is a structural property (greenfield / single-vendor brownfield / mixed brownfield), not a Microsoft-specific fact.
rationale: Microsoft is named as the assumed dominant supplier of the institution's identity/endpoint/observability estate. For an institution-agnostic reference, this presumes a specific market position. The trajectory itself is generalizable; only the vendor label is bound. Note this also recurs inside the matrix table cells.

rationale: Same Microsoft binding inside the table body. Detection-level: this is a concrete vendor name embedded in an institution-agnostic decision matrix.

location: ch04-self-assessment-EN.tex / Section: Reading the results (sec:sa-results), Table tab:sa-trajectory row 2 (Recommended trajectory cell)
proposedGenericDecision: Generalize 'Microsoft estate' to 'existing commercial-suite estate' or 'incumbent proprietary estate'.
rationale: Third Microsoft reference; same parameter. The architectural move (open plane in front of incumbent estate) is generic; the vendor name is not.

surfaceForm: The most common European starting point
location: ch04-self-assessment-EN.tex / Section: Reading the results (sec:sa-results), Table tab:sa-trajectory row 2 (Recommended trajectory cell)
proposedGenericDecision: Either drop the regional qualifier or parameterize the region so the claim ('most common starting point') is scoped to the deploying institution's market rather than hard-coded to Europe.
rationale: 'European' embeds the reference's home-region assumption. An institution-agnostic reference used outside Europe would find this empirical claim either wrong or unverifiable for its own market. Implicit jurisdiction/region binding.

location: ch04-self-assessment-EN.tex / Section: Reading the results (sec:sa-results), Table tab:sa-trajectory row 3 (Recommended trajectory cell)
proposedGenericDecision: Replace the US Carnegie 'R1' classification with a system-neutral descriptor such as 'research-intensive institutions' or 'doctoral research-intensive institutions'.
rationale: 'R1' is the US Carnegie Classification label. It is jurisdiction-bound terminology that does not exist in most other higher-education systems, making the reference implicitly US-anchored at this point. The substantive criterion (research intensity) is generic.

surfaceForm: the international peer comparison anticipated in phase~2 of the network of universities to which this Reference is addressed
location: ch04-self-assessment-EN.tex / Section: Re-assessment cadence (sec:sa-cadence), final paragraph
proposedGenericDecision: This presupposes a specific consortium/network of universities (and a phased programme) that owns the Reference. For an institution-agnostic instrument, generalize to 'any peer comparison the institution chooses to participate in' or parameterize the owning network/programme.
rationale: Implicit: assumes a concrete 'network of universities' as the addressee and a phased ('phase 2') roadmap. This binds the document to the originating UL-led consortium/programme context rather than to a generic adopting institution.

surfaceForm: one identity engineer, one network engineer, one security or governance representative, and one person familiar with procurement
location: ch04-self-assessment-EN.tex / Section: Purpose and method (sec:sa-purpose), paragraph 'Time and team'
proposedGenericDecision: Keep as role-based guidance (it is already role-based and not UL-specific), but flag that it presumes an institution large enough to staff four distinct specialist roles. Generic decision: retain; optionally note 'roles may be combined in smaller institutions'.
rationale: Mild implicit assumption of an institution with separable identity/network/security/procurement functions. Already role-based and broadly transferable; flagged only for completeness, low priority.

proposedGenericDecision: These glossary macros expand to standard, vendor- and institution-neutral technical terms. No generalization needed PROVIDED the shared glossary definitions are themselves agnostic. Verify each \gls expansion in the agnostic build does not embed a UL example.
rationale: Detection note per task scope ('a macro that expands to a UL term'): these are standard-acronym macros and almost certainly safe, but they are cross-file dependencies whose expansions must be confirmed agnostic. Low confidence that any binds to a UL term.

surfaceForm: a single canonical identity provider for the institution
location: ch04-self-assessment-EN.tex / Section: Section A --- Identity and federation maturity (sec:sa-identity), item A1
proposedGenericDecision: No change needed. The question is framed neutrally and applies to any institution regardless of campus/data-centre topology; it does not presume a single-campus model.
rationale: Considered for the 'single campus/data-centre' implicit-assumption category but rejected: the item asks whether identity is canonical vs fragmented, which is topology-independent. Recorded as a deliberate non-finding for audit traceability.
